newsitem.title: USA: S&P sees little impact from airport privatization.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees little impact from airport privatization.

text.p: Airports are increasingly privatizing services and facilities, but the practice has had little credit effect "positive or negative," Standard & Poor's Corp said Monday in CreditWeek Municipal.

"Under limited to more comprehensive privatization initiatives put forward so far, there has been no increased risk that is inconsistent with current credit quality of the airports Standard & Poor's rates," the agency said.

Standard & Poor's cited two examples of airport privatization -- Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport Authority, Calif., which has a limited operator agreement, and Indianapolis Airport Authority, which has a more comprehensive operator agreement with British Airports Authority USA.
The rating agency noted that none of the privatization benefits associated with those two airports "have been realized or are significant enough to warrant un upgrade."

"Credit quality could improve with increased efficiencies and cost savings while diversifying and improving nonairline revenues," Standard & Poor's said. "However, these benefits of privatization are likely to make a difference only if an airport is in competition with other facilities or perhaps has a high level of discretionary or connecting traffic."
